issues.legal_issue: A court on remand must comply with the remand order’s scope and cannot decide matters beyond the directions given.
A proposed amendment to pleadings at the appellate stage may be rejected where it is substantially delayed, lacks a sustainable explanation, and would require a fresh trial.

A transfer of rights in immovable property during litigation does not defeat the successful party’s rights in that property, though it does not make the transfer invalid between the transferor and transferee.
A suit to recover possession based on prior possession is maintainable even when the claimant does not assert ownership and the suit does not fall under Section 6 of the Specific Relief Act.
A defendant in a possession claim cannot defeat the claimant’s prior possession merely by asserting that a third party has a better right to possession.

A suit does not abate for failure to substitute every legal representative of a deceased defendant when the deceased’s interest is substantially represented by the remaining defendants who are also legal representatives.
Evidence cannot establish a defence on a point that was not raised in the pleadings.
Concurrent findings based on proper consideration of the record do not warrant interference under Article 136 absent perversity or patent illegality.
